content:
In 2021, Thomas Bloom answered several questions of Erdős and Graham regarding unit fractions. Then, he and Bhavik Mehta formalized the proof in Lean 3.42.1. The arxiv paper is available at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.03726 and includes this final paragraph:

This formalisation is a first in several respects: it is the first recent analytic number theory result to be formally verified; the first instance of the circle method; the first solution to a long-standing problem of Erdős. Part of the motivation for this formalisation was as a proof of concept: the Lean proof assistant and accompanying mathlib is advanced enough to make feasible the fast formalisation of new research results in mathematics, on the same timescale as the production of the ‘human-readable’ paper. Of course, this was made feasible by the relatively elementary and self-contained nature of the mathematics involved. Nonetheless, we believe that this arrangement, with a formal certificate of validation accompanying the human version of the paper, is a sign of things to come.

The original GitHub repo with the lean3 code is available here: https://github.com/b-mehta/unit-fractions

Using Codex from OpenAI, I have updated the code to compile under the latest Lean/Mathlib version 4.29.1 here: https://github.com/plby/unit-fractions/tree/master/src4

I have not (yet?) put any effort into cleaning up the code.

I would be happy to hear snappy names for the process of taking "bit rot" code and making it work again. Derotting? Bit revival? Bit revivification? Necromancing? Rehydrating? Bit compost?

There's snappy and there's appropriately descriptive. You are changing the code (writing code with the original as inspiration/blueprint) to meet present language/architectural constraints. I suggest "uptodating" for a neologism. (Say it quickly and with context to avoid being misconstrued.) Also, you are "uptodating the solution": code can be changed, but not properly "uptodate"ed if the architecture stays the same. (But the word and its usage can become yours when you provide the appropriate API for its use.)

content: Thanks for working on this, Boris! I'd be happy to update unit-fractions to Lean 4 with your code, though I'd (probably) like to make my own stylistic improvements before merging it into master. So a PR would be welcome.
